subject: StrideBank: urgent throughput degradation — fallback runbook and exec flag
messages:
From: Nicole Park <nicole.park@stridebank.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Kyle Roberts <kyle.roberts@stridebank.com>
Date: 2028-02-28T09:14:22Z
Subject: Production latency + error spike in Dedicated pool (StrideBank prod)

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a sustained rise in 95th/99th latency and an uptick in 502/503 errors across our production endpoints around 08:45 PST. Our telemetry shows request queueing on the dedicated GPU pool and timeouts on some signer calls. This is impacting customer-facing flows (loan quote generation).

Attachments: queue_snapshot-20280228.csv (summary of p95/p99 and error counts per minute)

Can you confirm whether this is an application-level degradation or something on Redwood's reserved capacity? We have a heavy batch of morning traffic but this looks like queue saturation rather than a one-off spike.

Nicole
VP Product
StrideBank

On a related note: we need an ETA and whether you can failover to the hosted tier while you remediate — we cannot accept sustained >500ms p95 for more than 20 minutes during business hours.
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Nicole Park <nicole.park@stridebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-28T09:37:08Z
Subject: Re: Production latency + error spike in Dedicated pool (StrideBank prod)

Nicole — thank you for the data and the quick heads-up. I pulled the attached snapshot and routed to infra immediately. Preliminary checks show the dedicated pool assigned to StrideBank hit sustained queue depth above the configured headroom threshold starting ~08:35 PST. We're seeing a combination of a traffic surge from a scheduled marketing campaign and suboptimal large-request batching from your runner.

Immediate next steps (what we're doing now):
- Engineers are increasing per-customer concurrency limits on the assigned pool to alleviate queueing (ETA 15m).
- Data plane will enable short-lived burst capacity to pull in 2 additional instances from shared burst (ETA 20m).
- We're preparing a fallback plan to redirect low-priority requests to our hosted tier by routing policy for up to 30 minutes if latency doesn't recover (need your approval).

Can you confirm if StrideBank can tolerate partial routing of non-auth-critical requests to hosted for 30 minutes? If yes, we'll start the policy push and I will escalate to leadership for expedited approval of credit/burst usage if needed.

I'm copying Marissa (ops lead) and Aditya (capacity) to keep them in the loop.

—Stephanie
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Nicole Park <nicole.park@stridebank.com>, Kyle Roberts <kyle.roberts@stridebank.com>
Date: 2028-02-28T10:02:50Z
Subject: Re: Production latency + error spike in Dedicated pool (StrideBank prod) — Exec flag

Team — quick summary for leadership and execs (flagging because this is a high-value account with reserved commit):
- Symptom: sustained queueing on reserved GPU pool assigned to StrideBank, p99 latency spiking to ~2.4s and 5xx rate up ~1.6% across endpoints since ~08:35 PST.
- Probable cause: traffic burst + large batched requests that maximize KV cache churn. Not a hardware failure; throughput ceiling hit for assigned capacity.
- Immediate mitigation in flight: increase per-customer concurrency, enable burst instances, and prepare request-level routing to hosted for low-priority paths.
- Business impact: potential SLA breach if not resolved within 30 minutes; may require short-term credit and temporary hosted routing.

Aditya — confirm that burst capacity allocation won't cause interference with higher-priority customers. Priyom — coordinate with Finance/Revenue Ops on temporary credit approval workflow; I will draft a short memo for the CRO.

Nicole/Kyle — can you provide a short list of endpoints we can safely reroute (e.g., background embedding jobs, async document enrichment) vs. those we must keep on your reserved pool? We'll only route non-blocking flows.

Marissa
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Nicole Park <nicole.park@stridebank.com>, Kyle Roberts <kyle.roberts@stridebank.com>, GCP Support <gcp-support@googlecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T15:02:05Z
Subject: Re: Production latency + error spike in Dedicated pool (StrideBank prod) — Mitigation completed

All — ops update: completed mitigation steps and post-mortem actions below. Posting final notes here for the thread and for Nicole/Kyle:

What we did (completed by 14:40 PST):
- Temporarily raised per-customer concurrency and bumped pool worker count via burst capacity. No interference observed with other reserved customers (burst came from shared pool 3).
- Deployed a routing policy to redirect low-priority endpoints to hosted tier for 30 minutes; reduction in p95/p99 within 8 minutes after policy.
- Tuned large-request batching on the customer agent (we pushed a short-lived patch to cap batch_size while we work on a longer fix).

Outcome: p99 latency back to ~210ms, 5xx rate down to 0.03%. StrideBank ops confirmed customer flows are nominal at 14:55 PST.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Priyom: draft credit memo and present to Revenue Ops by EOD tomorrow.
- Stephanie: work with StrideBank to create a list of safe-to-route endpoints and codify an automatic fallback policy (playbook in attached fallback_playbook_v1.pdf).
- Marissa/Aditya: schedule a dedicated capacity tuning review for StrideBank the week of Mar 5 to avoid recurrence (review batching patterns, KV cache sizing).

Nicole/Kyle — appreciate the quick collaboration. We'll keep the incident as an elevated customer item and follow up with a short RCA within 72 hours.

Cheers,
Aditya
Head of Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference
